original_source_first_claims.claim: Human learning task combines feature reward estimation with hypothesis or rule testing rather than presupposing a unique pure algorithm.
18 individual 30-trial games, with known vs unknown numbers of relevant stimulus dimensions and dimension counts one through three.
106 finished, 4 poor-performance excluded (threshold <0.468 reward), 102 analyzed; no separate causal neural recording.
Task stimuli choices use three multidimensional categorical visual features and probabilistic feedback on an unknown fixed conjunctive rewarding rule per game.
Nine one-dimensional, 27 two-dimensional and 27 three-dimensional hypotheses, unknown-D space 63; known-D restricts support to 9 or 27.
RL choice expected reward is the sum of learned feature values along corresponding object dimensions.
RL/other candidate choices via softmax inverse temperature β; fit probabilistic choice observations.
Feature value Rescorla–Wagner prediction error update selected feature; non-selected feature decay d, source alternative learning-rate distinctions.
Bayesian rule learning updates posterior p(h|choice/reward) over task-constrained full-rule hypotheses.
Bayesian rule learner choice expected reward integrates per-hypothesis reward likelihood; greedy for current trial only, not global game optimum.

original_source_first_claims.claim: Serial hypothesis tester latent currently tested hypothesis inferred from prior choices and reward observations using hidden-state/run-length posterior.
Known/unknown dimension instructions affect SHT initial hypothesis prior with dimensionality weights w_l and w_h.
Original SHT stay policy logistic in smoothed estimate (successes+1)/(tested+2) and choice noise; retain exact original conditional source units.
Random SHT alternate rule switch draws from task-prior alternatives under source exclusion conditions, no learned value-guided switch.
Hybrid guided SHT switches hypothesis based on learned featureRL values, coupling value learning and latent rule switching in source native original.
Original behavioral learning dynamics differ by number of relevant dimensions; no uniform strategy across 1D/2D/3D games.
Main original model candidate comparison: Bayesian rule, feature RL, random SHT, value-guided hybrid and approximate DQN benchmark.
Original main leave-one-game-out group predictive fit source values Bayesian .045±.003, featureRL .118±.008, random SHT .160±.009, hybrid .202±.009.
Even winning baseline hybrid does not reproduce participants' inferred number of relevant considered features accurately.
Full SHT variant joint optimization stay/testing/lapse/switch further improves test game predictive per-trial likelihood .033±.006 but retains number-of-features prediction failure.
Original source DQN trained on task to approximate reward maximum, not exact finite-horizon normative value iteration or global mathematical optimality.
Value-learning plus hypothesis-testing hybrid is limited, subject-level source fit does not uniquely prove human neural implementations or an exhaustive strategy search.
Supplement S1 Text models hidden hypothesis/run length recursion; p2 includes literal unresolved 'Equation ??' link, only confidently connect to main text Eqs8–10 by original prose.
Actual Dec 2022 correction changes funding acknowledgements only, retains November 2022 scientific equations, results and original mathematical interpretability.
Rule hypothesis testing accelerates learning in 1D; feature value learning contributes more when multidimensional reward structure makes exhaustive testing inefficient.
